text:
ana: Quick kickoff — customer asked for per-route cost attribution + trace hooks in Console so they can tie SLO regressions to $$ impact. Draft spec below, want alignment on rollout & launch criteria. High level: 1) per-route cost meter (tokens+compute), 2) lightweight trace hooks with adaptive sampling, 3) dashboard slices by route + model variant, 4) error analytics linked to cost spikes. Thoughts?

mike: Love it. Can you sketch acceptance criteria? Also: canary plan idea — 5% routes for 48h, compare p50/p95 latency + cost-per-1k-tokens to baseline. If regressions < 5% and cost change < 10% we promote.

sasha: Storage question — full traces for every request will explode retention costs. Need dedupe + compress and strict sampling defaults. Propose default 0.1% global + route overrides. Also retention: 14 days for full traces, 90 days for aggregated metrics.

praveen: Draft sampling config (for ops/devs):
```yaml
sampling_policy:
  default: 0.001 # 0.1%
  routes:
    /v1/generate: 0.01
    /v1/embeddings: 0.0005
  conditions:
    error: 1.0 # always sample errors
    anomaly: 1.0 # always sample if cost spike detected
```
This lets us collect errors + anomalies while keeping volume sane. We should expose a per-project override in the Console.

joan: Two product constraints: 1) Customers will want RBAC on cost views (billing teams vs devs). 2) For regulated customers, traces may contain PII — need redaction hooks & KMS key tagging before retention. Add that to launch blockers.

ana: (typo — meant ana) Proposed launch criteria:
- Functional: route-level cost + token breakdown appears in Console for top-10 routes
- Reliability: instrumentation adds <10% CPU overhead on dataplane under typical load
- Quality: no error-rate uplift >0.1pp during canary
- Economics: telemetry storage costs within projected budget (< +12% infra spend for first quarter)
- Security: redaction + KMS tagging present for Private deployments
- UX: one dashboard template + query builder snippet + short migration guide
- Rollout: canary (5% traffic x 48h) -> 25% x 72h -> GA; manual kill-switch & auto-roll-back on SLO breaches

mike: I'll own canary monitoring and create a temporary dashboard showing: per-route p50/p95, cost-per-1k, error-rate, sampling-rate. Will add alert if cost-per-1k deviates > 20% or error-rate increases >0.5pp.

sasha: Re: retention + cost — engineering asks: what's allowed max storage delta we can target for engineering to tune? Product: need an explicit budget delta number.

ana: (again ana) Product budget suggestion: aim for <+12% infra spend, with a hard guardrail of +25% requiring exec signoff. If we hit >+18% during canary, we pause and investigate.

praveen: Small perf note: tracing hooks should be async and write to a write-ahead queue; apply per-route sampling before any expensive serialization. Suggest adding a lightweight proto envelope to minimize overhead.

observability-bot: created issue #4532: "per-route-cost-traces - sampling + RBAC + redaction" and assigned to @ana, @mike, @sasha. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/issues/4532

joan: Final question — priority vs other Console items? If this is customer-driven (big customer asking), we should list it as P0 for next quarter and attach the customer vignette. Otherwise P1.

ana: It's driven by a top-10 customer with enterprise SLA ask. Recommend P0. Next steps:
- Mike: dashboard + canary monitoring (owner) — due EOD next Wed
- Praveen: instrument perf guardrails + async proto plan — PR proto by next Tue
- Sasha: retention & cost modelling + storage budget calc — due in 3 days
- Joan: prepare customer vignette + RBAC compliance checklist — due 5 days
I'll book a 30m sync after initial artifacts land. Thanks! :thumbsup:
